newsitem.title: MALI: Mali opposition says election boycott respected.
newsitem.headline: Mali opposition says election boycott respected.

text.p: Mali's mainstream opposition parties on Monday said their boycott of Sunday presidential elections had been respected after a low turnout in the impoverished West African country.

"Mali had never seen such a low level of participation," said Mountaga Tall, speaking for 22 parties who boycotted the poll, leaving President Alpha Oumar Konare with only one challenger -- businessman Mamadou Maribatrou Diaby.
Tall put the turnout figure at "less than 20 percent" in the second multiparty presidential elections since independence from France in 1960, which are seen as a key test of democracy.
No official turnout figure, or result, has yet been given.
Witnesses said turnout was low, in contrast to a chaotic April 13 parliamentary election which prompted the opposition to demand that this year's national elections be suspended and reorganised.
Konare, a historian elected in 1992 during Mali's widely praised democratic transition, promised to form a broad-based government after the election.
Tall said that when Konare's mandate from the 1992 election expires on June 8, Mali would be "without a president" as far as the opposition was concerned.
